correctness.rationale: Under reversal the pair (M,S) has the same law as (S-m,S). Under global sign change it has the same law as (-m,-S). For odd g this gives E[M g(S)]=E[(S-m)g(S)] and E[M g(S)]=E[m g(S)], hence twice the first expectation equals E[S g(S)]. The covariance and range/drawdown identities are algebraic consequences. The iid correlation limit is separately justified by Donsker convergence plus maximal-moment uniform integrability.

value.rationale: The maximum, endpoint, drawdown, and range are canonical finite-horizon fluctuation statistics. The theorem exposes an exact structural relation that persists for dependent nonexchangeable paths, clarifying which part of the familiar iid joint behavior comes only from two elementary symmetries. The odd-transform extension provides a reusable family of mixed-moment identities rather than a single isolated covariance.
